questions.question:
The DevOps team would like to get the list of all Namespaces in the cluster.

The list can contain other columns like STATUS or AGE.

Save the list to `/tmp/exam/1/namespaces`.

verification.description: Namespaces list file exists with correct content

questions.question:
Create a single Pod named `pod1` in the `default` namespace.

The Pod should use image `httpd:2.4.41-alpine` and the container should be named `pod1-container`.

In Namespace `neptune`, create a Job named `neb-new-job` that runs image `busybox:1.31.0`.

The Job should execute the command: `sleep 2 && echo done`

It should be created from the yaml template available at `/tmp/exam/3/job.yaml`.

Edit and apply the yaml template to create the Job.

Team Mercury needs to perform Helm operations on their namespace.

1. Uninstall the Helm release named `internal-issue-report-apiv1` from namespace `mercury`

2. Upgrade the Helm release named `internal-issue-report-apiv2` to version 2.0.0 in namespace `mercury`

Note: There is a Helm repository already configured named `killershell` available at `http://localhost:6000`.

verification.description: Second Helm release is upgraded correctly

questions.question:
In Namespace `neptune`, there is a ServiceAccount named `neptune-sa-v2`.

Extract the token from the Secret associated with this ServiceAccount and save it to `/tmp/exam/5/token`.

Note: ServiceAccounts automatically create associated Secrets that contain tokens.

verification.description: Token file exists with valid token

questions.question:
Create a Pod named `pod6` in the `default` namespace using image `busybox:1.31.0`.

The Pod should have a readiness probe that:
- Executes the command: `cat /tmp/ready`
- Has an initialDelaySeconds of 5
- Has a periodSeconds of 10

The container should run the command: `touch /tmp/ready && sleep 1d`

verification.description: Pod exists with correct readiness probe configuration

questions.question:
The webserver `my-happy-shop` is currently running in namespace `saturn`.

Team Saturn needs to move this webserver to namespace `neptune` for better organization.

1. Get the yaml of the existing Pod `my-happy-shop` from namespace `saturn`
2. Modify it to run in namespace `neptune`
3. Delete the old Pod from `saturn`
4. Create the new Pod in `neptune`

verification.description: Pod no longer exists in saturn namespace
Pod exists in neptune namespace with same configuration

questions.question:
In namespace `neptune`, there is a Deployment named `neptune-deployment`.

1. Check the history of this Deployment to find the revision number that introduced a specific change
2. Rollback the Deployment to revision 1
3. Update the Deployment to use image `httpd:2.4.41-alpine`
4. Scale the Deployment to 4 replicas

verification.description: Deployment has correct image and replicas

questions.question:
In namespace `pluto`, create a Deployment named `project-plt-6cc-api`.

Deployment specifications:
- Image: `nginx:1.17.3-alpine`
- Replicas: 1
- Container name: `api`
- Security Context for container: Run as user 10000 and group 20000, Capabilities: drop ALL
- Resource Limits: memory 20Mi
- Resource Requests: memory 20Mi

In namespace `pluto`, there is a Deployment named `project-earthflower`.

1. Create a ClusterIP Service named `project-plt-6cc-svc` that exposes this Deployment on port 3333, targeting port 80
2. Get the logs from one of the Deployment's Pods and save them to `/tmp/exam/10/logs`

In the `default` namespace, there is a Pod named `holy-api` running.

1. Get the name of the container running in this Pod and save it to `/tmp/exam/11/container-name`
2. Execute the command `date` inside the running container and save the output to `/tmp/exam/11/date-output`

In namespace `earth`, create a PersistentVolume named `earth-project-earthflower-pv`.

PersistentVolume specifications:
- Capacity: 2Gi
- Access Mode: ReadWriteOnce
- Host Path: /tmp/exam-pv
- Storage Class Name: shared-host-path

Then create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `earth-project-earthflower-pvc` in namespace `earth`.

PersistentVolumeClaim specifications:
- Request: 2Gi
- Access Mode: ReadWriteOnce
- Storage Class Name: shared-host-path

In namespace `moon`, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `moon-pvc-126`.

PersistentVolumeClaim specifications:
- Storage Class: moon-retain
- Access Mode: ReadWriteOnce
- Storage Request: 3Gi

Ensure the PVC binds successfully. If no suitable PV exists, create one that matches the requirements.

In namespace `moon`, there is a Secret named `secret-handler` with the following keys:
- `user`
- `pass`
- `id`

Create a Pod named `secret-handler` using image `bash:5.0.11`.

The Pod should:
1. Make the secret available as environment variables:
   - SECRET_USER from key `user`
   - SECRET_PASS from key `pass`
2. Mount the secret key `id` to path `/tmp/secret-id`
3. Run the command: `bash -c 'sleep 1d'`

verification.description: Pod exists with environment variables configured
Secret is mounted correctly as file

questions.question:
In namespace `moon`, there is a ConfigMap named `configmap-web-moon-html`.

Create a Pod named `web-moon` using image `nginx:1.17.3-alpine`.

The Pod should mount the ConfigMap as a volume at path `/usr/share/nginx/html` so that the nginx server serves the content from the ConfigMap.

verification.description: Pod exists and ConfigMap is mounted correctly

questions.question:
In namespace `mercury`, there is a Deployment named `check-ip`.

The logs for this Deployment should be collected and saved.

1. Add a sidecar container named `logger` to the Deployment's Pod template
2. The sidecar should use image `busybox:1.31.0`
3. The sidecar should run the command: `sh -c 'tail -f /var/log/check-ip.log'`
4. Both containers should share a volume named `logger-volume` mounted at `/var/log`
5. The main container should write logs to `/var/log/check-ip.log`

Save the updated Deployment yaml to `/tmp/exam/16/check-ip-deployment.yaml` and apply it.

Create a Pod named `holy-api-v2` in the `default` namespace.

The Pod should have:
1. An initContainer named `init-container` that:
   - Uses image `busybox:1.31.0`
   - Runs the command: `sh -c 'echo Init done > /tmp/init-done.txt'`
   - Mounts a volume named `workdir` at `/tmp`

2. A main container named `main-container` that:
   - Uses image `nginx:1.17.3-alpine`
   - Mounts the same volume `workdir` at `/tmp`

The volume should be an emptyDir.

verification.description: Pod has init container and main container configured correctly

questions.question:
In namespace `mars`, create a Deployment named `manager-mars-api`.

Deployment specifications:
- Image: `httpd:2.4-alpine`
- Replicas: 3

Then create a Service named `manager-api-svc` that:
- Type: NodePort
- Port: 4444 (Service port)
- Target Port: 80 (Container port)
- NodePort: 30080 (fixed NodePort)
- Selector: Should match the Deployment's Pods

In namespace `jupiter`, there are several Services and Deployments.

1. Create a temporary Pod using image `busybox:1.31.0` with the command `wget -O- service-name:port`
2. Test the connectivity to Service `manager-api-svc` on port 4444 and save the output to `/tmp/exam/19/service-test`
3. Get the ClusterIP of the Service and save it to `/tmp/exam/19/cluster-ip`

verification.description: ClusterIP file exists with correct IP

questions.question:
In namespace `venus`, there are two Deployments: `api` and `frontend`.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `np1` that:
1. Applies to Pods with label `component: frontend`
2. Allows ingress traffic from Pods with label `component: api` on port 80
3. Denies all other ingress traffic

Note: The Deployments are already labeled appropriately.

In namespace `neptune`, create a Deployment named `neptune-10ab`.

Deployment specifications:
- Image: `httpd:2.4-alpine`
- Replicas: 3
- Container name: `neptune-pod-10ab`
- ServiceAccount: `neptune-sa-v2` (already exists)
- Resource Requests:
  - Memory: 20Mi
- Resource Limits:
  - Memory: 50Mi

verification.description: Deployment exists with correct basic configuration
Resource limits and requests are configured correctly

questions.question:
In namespace `sun`, there are many Pods with different labels.

1. Add the label `protected: true` to all Pods that have label `type: worker` or `type: runner`
2. Save the list of Pods with label `protected=true` to `/tmp/exam/22/protected-pods`

Note: The Pods already exist with various labels including `type=worker`, `type=runner`, `type=test`, etc.

questions.question:
PREVIEW QUESTION 1: Liveness Probe

In namespace `pluto`, there is a Deployment named `project-23-api`.

Team Pluto needs it to be more reliable. Implement a liveness probe which checks the container to be reachable on port 80.

1. Get the current Deployment yaml and save to `/tmp/exam/23/project-23-api.yaml`
2. Add a TCP liveness probe on port 80 with:
   - initialDelaySeconds: 10
   - periodSeconds: 15
3. Save the modified yaml to `/tmp/exam/23/project-23-api-new.yaml`
4. Apply the changes

verification.description: Deployment has liveness probe configured correctly
